_about: Cloud 2026-11-03. IELTS exams 7-10: the Common mistake pair on key point 3 (the trap / language point), written as a mini exam item. Academic explain only (gt:false).

x07-l1.wrong: A kitchen needs a kettle, so you write 'kettle' before you hear it.
x07-l1.right: She says 'we've already got a kettle; what we need is a toaster' - toaster.

x07-l2.wrong: 'Visitors usually head for the mosaic' - you label the mosaic as the first stop.
x07-l2.right: 'but we'll start at the bath house' - follow the route the speaker takes, not what people usually do.

x07-l3.wrong: Option A is true (the guides are long), so you choose A.
x07-l3.right: The question asks what the students will change. A is true but not the answer; they will change the pace: B.

x07-l4.wrong: 'Scissors, for example' - you write 'scissors' in the gap for the main problem.
x07-l4.right: 'but the biggest issue is desks' - the gap wants the main point, not the first example.

x07-r1.wrong: 'The tin can was invented in France.' The passage: a Frenchman invented canning - TRUE.
x07-r1.right: Canning is not the tin can. The passage names an Englishman for the can - FALSE.

x07-r2.wrong: Paragraph B mentions carbon storage, so its heading is 'How seagrass stores carbon'.
x07-r2.right: One mention is a detail. The whole paragraph is about why the meadows are disappearing: choose that heading.

x07-r3.wrong: 'Zhang believes robots will replace couriers' - so the writer believes it.
x07-r3.right: That is Zhang's claim. Match it to Zhang, and keep looking for the writer's own view.

x07-s.wrong: I worked hard and it was good.
x07-s.right: I spent three weekends rebuilding the shelves, and in the end the shop could open on time.

x07-w1.wrong: The pie chart increased from 20% to 35%.
x07-w1.right: Adults made up 20% of visitors in 2010 and 35% in 2020.

x07-w2.wrong: Cheap flights have advantages and disadvantages. Both are important.
x07-w2.right: Although cheap flights bring tourism income, the environmental cost outweighs it.

x08-l1.right: ThirTEENTH = 13th; THIRtieth = 30th. Listen for the stress, and check it against the day of the week.

x08-l2.wrong: The box has 'free parking', so one answer must be free parking.
x08-l2.right: Two options in the box are never used. Only match what the speaker actually says about each stand.

x08-l3.wrong: You hear 'handwritten' in option A, so A.
x08-l3.right: She says 'handwritten notes took too long, so I switched to typing' - the answer is typing, C.

x08-l4.wrong: 'Most people think the birds leave because of the cold' - you write 'cold'.
x08-l4.right: 'In fact it's the lack of food' - the answer is 'food'.

x08-r1.wrong: 'The designer studied in Paris.' The passage says she worked in Paris - TRUE.
x08-r1.right: Working there is not studying there. The passage does not say where she studied - NOT GIVEN.

x08-r2.wrong: Section C says 'residents fear losing their homes', so the writer predicts homes will be lost.
x08-r2.right: That is the residents' voice. The writer's view comes with 'I' or 'in my view'.

x08-r3.wrong: Both section D and the statement are about donkeys guarding sheep, so D.
x08-r3.right: The statement is about donkeys attacking foxes; that detail is in section F.

x08-s.wrong: She said me she is tired.
x08-s.right: She told me she was tired.

x08-w1.wrong: After that, they are pressing the pulp and then dry.
x08-w1.right: Next, the pulp is pressed, and then it is dried.

x08-w2.wrong: Fashion furniture is bad. People should buy classic furniture. Fashion furniture is bad for the planet.
x08-w2.right: Fashionable furniture is cheap and fun, but because it is replaced so often, the waste it creates outweighs the benefits.

x09-l1.wrong: 'Teachers can park on site' - you write that students can park on site.
x09-l1.right: The rule for students is different: 'students use the public car park'. Match the rule to the right group.

x09-l2.wrong: 'The cafe is opposite the gate' - you label the cafe next to the gate.
x09-l2.right: Opposite = across from, facing. Next to = beside. Check each position word before you write the letter.

x09-l3.wrong: 'We could survey the whole school' - you choose 'survey'.
x09-l3.right: 'but that's far too many people, so interviews with ten pupils' - the final plan is the answer.

x09-l4.wrong: 'Archaeologists assumed the boat was Roman' - you write Roman.
x09-l4.right: 'Carbon dating showed it was Bronze Age' - the fact comes second: Bronze Age.

x09-r1.wrong: 'Cushioned shoes reduce injuries.' The passage says they feel softer - TRUE.
x09-r1.right: Feeling softer is not reducing injuries. The passage does not say that - NOT GIVEN.

x09-r2.wrong: 'Smugglers used caves to hide goods' is well known, so TRUE.
x09-r2.right: Only what the passage says counts. If the passage never mentions caves - NOT GIVEN.

x09-r3.wrong: 'Rumours spread faster online.' The writer says many people believe this - YES.
x09-r3.right: 'Many people believe' is not the writer's view. His own line says the evidence is mixed - NOT GIVEN.

x09-s.wrong: The rule is no cars in the centre. It is good.
x09-s.right: Cars are banned from the centre after 10 a.m., so the square is quieter and the cafes have put tables outside.

x09-w1.wrong: Yoga rose and football fell and dance was 40.
x09-w1.right: Yoga rose from 10% to 25%, overtaking football, which fell to 15%.

x09-w2.wrong: Some people think competition is good. I think so too.
x09-w2.right: Supporters of competition argue it raises standards. However, in my experience, teamwork produces better results.

x10-l1.wrong: Locker code: 4719, the first number you hear.
x10-l1.right: 'We changed all the codes last week; it's 4791 now' - the current code is the answer.

x10-l2.wrong: She mentions goggles, so the advice is 'buy goggles'.
x10-l2.right: She says 'don't buy goggles yet; just bring a towel' - the advice given is 'bring a towel'.

x10-l3.wrong: The library is open late, so the comment about the library is 'convenient hours'.
x10-l3.right: The students' point is that its books are out of date. A true detail is not the comment.

x10-l4.wrong: 'Hedges were planted mainly for shade - sorry, for shelter' - you write 'shade'.
x10-l4.right: The word after the correction is the answer: 'shelter'.

x10-r1.wrong: 'Queen bumblebees die in winter.' The passage: 'workers die in autumn' - TRUE.
x10-r1.right: Workers are not queens. The passage says queens hibernate - FALSE.

x10-r2.wrong: 'Divers often claim...' - match it to Dr Ruiz, the only diver named.
x10-r2.right: 'Divers often claim' is a group voice. Only match a named person to what that person says.

x10-r3.wrong: 'Kindness is learned, not natural.' The writer discusses both ideas - NOT GIVEN.
x10-r3.right: The writer ends 'the evidence points to an instinct' - NO.

x10-s.wrong: The view was very beautiful and amazing.
x10-s.right: From the balcony you could see the whole bay, with fishing boats coming in at sunset.

x10-w1.right: The share of teenagers taking music lessons rose to 30% in 2020.

x10-w2.wrong: Fast food has good points and bad points.
x10-w2.right: Global chains bring jobs and choice, but these gains are smaller than the loss of local food traditions.
